summary: Admit material file renames in pre-commit hooks

delivery.outcome: Admit material renames, bound immutable source reads and run the same adoption cases as separate mandatory bounded CI/Goal checks.
nonGoals: No consumer hook edits or activation before a published immutable adoption.
No release/version changes or writes to ticket-429 scope.
No weakening of writer, pin, overlap, review or governance-only transition checks.

architecture.decision: Include Git rename records in the existing NUL-delimited material-deliverable scan; exercise both real hooks in isolated Git fixtures with deterministic rename detection. Retain the separate governance-only DRC refusal. Read immutable source blobs through one NUL-framed Git batch per invocation; cache only literal immutable revision data within that invocation. Keep target-state and publication validation live. Move four identical Python invocations from the aggregate adoption shell suite into four mandatory shell suites; wire every suite explicitly in the existing protected Linux CI job. Keep the same300s per-command limit and every Windows check. The next observed aggregate also combines a33-case279s allocation module with six other Python modules and its core scenarios. Preserve these seven selections and their private TMPDIR/Git-discovery boundary in seven separately mandatory checks. The containment regression now anchors at the unchanged executable fixture-creation boundary instead of the moved allocation invocation; its real absolute/relative caller-preservation checks are unchanged.
interfaceChanges: Existing Linux CI test job runs the same four Python suites as separate mandatory shell checks; protected context names and Windows validation unchanged.
architecture.rollback: Independently reviewed revert; preserve ticket branches and immutable adopted releases.

validation.evidence: Pure and edited source/test renames pass in both real hook variants; the same regressions fail on the accepted base.
Carrier-only renames and inactive implementation renames remain rejected with canonical diagnostics.
Canonical governance and publication gates pass before exact-head OneDev and independent approval.

Real review has bounded Git process count with identical payloads; binary/unusual paths, missing blobs, malformed responses and hostile Git environment remain fail-closed. Existing migration/security regressions remain mandatory.
Exact original four Python selections are each wired once; complete Goal discovery and protected Linux CI execute all suites, with the existing300s per-command bound and no coverage skips.

Seven original Python invocations and private fixture/Git-ceiling environment are retained; actual Goal and Linux CI require every new suite; source default timeout remains300s and Windows check is unchanged.
